content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text makes Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because its passive verb and feminine relative admit two readings, which is the verse-admits-two-senses ground K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"“A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand” — weighed as barring UNDERDETERMINED when a verse is said to admit two readings versus applying only where one verse’s words have two simultaneous senses.","why":"It grounds UNDERDETERMINED on Matthew 1:16 admitting both readings, contrary to K-S2’s command that a verse carrying two senses at once is not open and both senses stand."}
